news.title: Messi sizzles with record double in first start since World Cup final
news.lede: Lionel Messi became the all-time leading scorer in the Leagues Cup after netting twice in Inter Miami's 4-2 victory over Atlético de San Luis today (Bangladesh time) in the 2026 edition's opening group matches. The Argentine superstar cancelled out the visitors' early opener in the 11th minute, finishing from Noah Allen's pass before Telasco Segovia put Miami ahead. Messi struck again just before half-time, once more converting an Allen assist, to take his Leagues Cup tally to 14 goals -- the most in the competition's history. Messi had helped Inter Miami win the 2023 Leagues Cup shortly after joining the club.

news.title: How to fix Fifa: what can be done to salvage football’s beleaguered governing body?
news.lede: Gianni Infantino followed World Cup controversies with a widely scorned plan to let private investors in. Here’s how the game’s leaders can find a path forward. How can an organisation that runs the biggest sporting event in the world also be the one that sets the rules for the entire game? We saw the reality of such a conflict at the recent World Cup as Fifa ran roughshod over its rulebook – be it over the length of suspensions or the duration of half-time – in an attempt to generate more attention for its competition.

news.title: Ferran Torres' Barcelona future uncertain after comments spark backlash
news.lede: Ferran Torres has made 207 appearances for Barcelona since signing from Manchester City in 2022 but 94 (45%) have been as a substitute. Ferran Torres will return to Barcelona later this month having cemented his name in the country's football folklore following his extra-time winner to seal Spain's second World Cup triumph. His profile and marketability has significantly grown and those around him will be keen to ensure he makes the most of a career-defining moment. But a summer dominated by World Cup celebrations has given way to transfer speculation, fuelled by the forward's own comments during a media tour in the United States.

news.title: Police raid South Korea FA in investigation into World Cup coach appointment
news.lede: Police raided South Korea’s football association on Thursday as part of an investigation into the appointment of the coach in charge during their dismal World Cup campaign. Officers conducted “search and seizure operations” at the Korea Football Association (KFA) headquarters, looking into allegations of “obstruction of business” in the recruitment of former coach Hong Myung-bo, a police spokesman said. The 57-year-old Hong resigned in June after South Korea were knocked out at the group stage of the 48-team showpiece in the United States, Mexico and Canada following a shock 1-0 defeat to South Africa. Questions were already dogging the KFA over the 2024 appointment of Hong, but scrutiny has intensified since the team failed to make the last-32 knockout stage.

news.title: World Cup heartbreak in the past, Lionel Messi unleashes magic for Inter Miami
news.lede: Lionel Messi scored twice and helped Inter Miami beat Atletico San Luis 4-2 in their Leagues Cup opener. news.title: Players who turned World Cup heroics into big transfers
news.lede: Vozinha, James Rodriguez and Mesut Ozil all earned big moves after standout performances at a World Cup. The World Cup is football's biggest stage, filled with goals, drama and unforgettable moments - but it can also prove to be the ultimate shop window. World Cup heroics have transformed players' lives in the past, and Vozinha's recent move to Chilean side Colo-Colo after an impressive tournament with Cape Verde is the latest reminder that the competition still has the power to change careers. At the age of 40, the goalkeeper's journey from the Portuguese second division to Chile's biggest club may be unique, but he is not the first to get a big move after starring on the global stage.

news.title: FIFA backs Infantino and apologises over failed World Cup plan
news.lede: In a statement, FIFA's leadership acknowledged "that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media". "Following a meeting in Rabat, Morocco, the FIFA Secretary General and members of the FIFA Management Board in attendance reaffirmed their full support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, as the only official elected by the 211 FIFA Member Associations," the statement added. Infantino has come under increasing pressure, even from within his organisation, over his handling of the proposal, and calls for him to step down have grown since he abandoned it last Saturday. FIFA floated the plan, saying it could raise up to $4.2 billion based on a valuation of $20 billion for a new commercial subsidiary, called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which it proposed would run events such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.
